brief.headline: This supplier is in the distress zone and losing money — lead with supply security and qualifying a second source, not a hard price squeeze; you're 7.21% of their sales, so you have leverage, but use it carefully.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹1.62/NOS we pay Bprex for the same LDPE bottle, closing the 4.3% gap.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS for LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE, saving ₹3.37 L/year
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Bprex ₹1.62/NOS for this item; Berry charges ₹1.69/NOS — a 4.3% premium with no clear reason. They're a reseller (100.0% traded goods), so their price carries a margin; push them to match the best price we pay or explain the difference.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (15 days after receipt instead of 30) in return for a 2–3% price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster ties up ₹3.34 L of our cash, so the price cut must cover that cost and deliver a net saving.

brief.financialLeverage: Berry is fragile: they lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24, keep -199.2% of every ₹100 they sell (similar firms keep 2.3%), owe 220.44x their own cash, and sit in the distress zone (Altman Z -0.18). Their cash is stuck for 335d vs 70d for peers, so cash is very tight. But you're a big customer — your ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr in sales — so they need you. Use that leverage gently: frame the ask around keeping your business and helping them turn cash faster, not a hard squeeze that tips them over. Line up a second source now — if they can't deliver or go under, you need a Plan B ready to roll.

evidence.point: You're paying ₹3.37 L/year more than the best price you already have
Berry charges ₹1.69/NOS for LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE; Bprex delivers it at ₹1.62/NOS — a 4.3% gap
Your ₹81.39 L annual spend is 7.21% of everything they sell
They lost money last year and keep far less than their peers
Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
They are 100.0% a reseller — so their price includes a trading margin you can push on

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) with pharma bottles, caps and preforms — a strong, stable second source.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) covering bottles and closures — robust alternate for your 5 mL bottles.

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already supplies the same LDPE bottle at ₹1.62/NOS — your current benchmark and a proven fallback.

risks: Berry sits in the distress zone (Altman Z -0.18) and lost ₹-22.50 Cr last year — steady supply is at risk; don't load more volume on them without a qualified backup in parallel.
Their overall money-health score is 1/10 — among the weakest you'll see; treat them as high-risk and keep safety stock or a dual-source plan.
Pushing too hard on price could break a fragile supplier; frame your ask as 'help us keep buying from you' and tie any discount to faster payment or a firmer forecast.
They are 100.0% a reseller, not a maker — if their upstream source changes terms or stops supply, your line stops; always have a direct manufacturer (like Manjushree or Mold-Tek) as Plan B.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying 4.3% more for the 5 mL bottle than we do elsewhere — let's close that gap and talk about how faster payment or a firmer forecast can help your cash flow, so we both win.
